channel.title: Cadence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 50 sources.

item.title: Advancing Payment: What the Proposed 2027 Medicare Fee Schedule Means for PTs
item.description: APTA has released an analysis of the proposed 2027 Medicare Physician Fee Schedule, highlighting key provisions affecting physical therapists' payment and practice, with a call for member comments by Sept. 14.
item.author: APTA

item.title: Modest Payment Increases Finalized by CMS for SNFs and IRFs
item.description: CMS finalized modest payment increases for Skilled Nursing Facilities (SNFs) and Inpatient Rehabilitation Facilities (IRFs) for fiscal year 2027, while introducing earlier deadlines for care initiation and interdisciplinary team meetings for IRFs, and requiring all-payer Minimum Data Set submissions for SNFs starting October 1.
item.author: APTA

item.title: Foot-Targeted Rehabilitation for Pronation-Related Anterior Knee Pain: A Two-Phase Case-Control Study and Single-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial of Manual Therapy Versus Neuromuscular Training Each With Augmented Low-Dye Taping.
item.description: A two-phase study including an RCT compared manual therapy plus augmented low-dye taping (MT + ALDT) and neuromuscular training plus ALDT (NMT + ALDT) for pronation-related anterior knee pain, demonstrating short-term effectiveness.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Focal Muscle Vibration for Upper Limb Spasticity After Stroke: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of studies (inception-March 2026) involving adults with post-stroke upper limb spasticity found focal muscle vibration (FMV) has a significant effect (Hedges' g=0.74, 95% CI 0.52-0.97) on reducing spasticity.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: The Optimal Exercise Modality and Dose for Blood Pressure Management in Middle-Aged and Older Adults: A Systematic Review with Bayesian Model-Based, and Dose-Response Network Meta-Analysis of RCTs.
item.description: This systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis of RCTs identified optimal exercise modalities and doses for lowering resting systolic and diastolic BP in middle-aged and older adults (≥45 years) by May 2025.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Biofeedback in Parkinson's disease: A systematic review with meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review with meta-analysis of randomized trials found that adding biofeedback to practice effectively improves lower limb activity in people with Parkinson's disease compared to practice alone.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Physical Therapy Management of Fall Risk in Community-Dwelling Older Adults (CPG+)
item.description: APTA Geriatrics has released an updated clinical practice guideline for physical therapy management of fall risk in community-dwelling adults aged 65 and over, replacing the 2015 version and effective April 1, 2025.
item.author: APTA

item.title: Carrying an unseen weight: the neuro-perceptual landscape of limb heaviness after stroke- a scoping review.
item.description: This scoping review maps the evidence on perceived limb heaviness after stroke, identifying it as an under-recognized symptom associated with altered sensorimotor integration, impaired proprioception, and disrupted body representation, which current assessments often miss.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: White Matter Diffusion Anisotropy and the Effects of Inpatient Multidisciplinary Rehabilitation in Parkinson's Disease: A Diffusion Tensor Imaging Analysis.
item.description: This study investigated whether pretreatment corticospinal tract (CST) fractional anisotropy (FA) predicts inpatient rehabilitation response in 94 Parkinson's disease patients. Patients were classified as responders (UPDRS Part III improvement ≥2.5 points; n=61) or non-responders (n=33).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Clinical and neurophysiological determinants of response to contralesional low-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation after stroke: A systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis confirmed the efficacy of contralesional low-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (LF-rTMS) for post-stroke upper-limb rehabilitation and identified baseline motor impairment severity and corticospinal tract integrity as key modifiers of treatment effects.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Comparative effectiveness of exercise-based prehabilitation before total knee arthroplasty: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
item.description: A systematic review and network meta-analysis compared the effectiveness of various exercise-based prehabilitation modalities before total knee arthroplasty, aiming to clarify optimal approaches.
item.author: BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil

item.title: Effect of kinesiology taping on limb oedema in patients with severe hyper-dependency using shear-wave elastography: a randomized clinical trial.
item.description: A randomized clinical trial (n=50) demonstrated that kinesiology taping at 25% tension significantly reduced the elastic coefficient of the dermis layer in limb oedema patients compared to 0% tension taping at day 9, assessed by shear-wave elastography.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Prestroke Rehabilitation Reserve and Mobility and Self-Care Outcomes After Incident Stroke Across Four International Aging Cohorts.
item.description: A harmonized longitudinal cohort study (N=7486, mean age 70.0 years) across four international aging cohorts found that lower multidimensional pre-stroke rehabilitation reserve was associated with adverse mobility and self-care status after incident stroke.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparison of high-intensity laser therapy and extracorporeal shock wave therapy for the treatment of plantar flexor spasticity in post-stroke patients.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial with 42 stroke patients compared high-intensity laser therapy (HILT) and radial extracorporeal shock wave therapy (rESWT) as adjunctive treatments for plantar flexor spasticity, with both groups showing greater improvements than rehabilitation alone.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: A grade-specific clinical prediction rule for independent walking after traumatic spinal cord injury.
item.description: A clinical prediction rule was developed using the National Spinal Cord Injury Statistical Centre dataset (2607 patients) to predict independent walking one year after traumatic spinal cord injury, with differentiated prognoses for individual ASIA Impairment Scale grades.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Extended-Window Thrombolysis Improves Stroke Outcomes with increased bleeding risk: JAMA
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 14 RCTs (N=4,174) found that intravenous thrombolysis given ≥4.5 hours after acute ischemic stroke onset improved functional outcomes (NNT 12–16) but increased symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage (RR 2.44, NNH 62).
item.author: Medical Dialogues

item.title: Application of non-invasive electroencephalogram-based brain-computer interfaces in post-stroke hand function rehabilitation.
item.description: This article reviews the application of non-invasive EEG-based brain-computer interfaces (BCI) in post-stroke hand function rehabilitation, explaining how BCI decodes imagined hand movements to drive exoskeletons, FES, or VR, thereby strengthening neural pathways and promoting motor recovery.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Development and psychometric validation of the shoulder problems assessment scale.
item.description: Researchers developed and validated the 12-item Shoulder Problems Assessment Scale (SPAS), an activity-based PROM using a hierarchical stepwise yes/no format, with field testing on 415 patients at 12 outpatient PT centers.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Arm exercise training in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
item.description: An umbrella review synthesizing six databases up to May 2026 concluded that arm exercise training is a valuable component of pulmonary rehabilitation for COPD patients, addressing extrapulmonary features and skeletal muscle dysfunction.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: More Than Just Arm Movement: Finger-Worn Accelerometers Provide a Valid and Sensitive Alternative to Wrist-Worn Accelerometers for Measuring Real-World Upper-Limb Performance in Stroke Survivors
item.description: Finger-worn accelerometers provided a valid and sensitive alternative to wrist-worn accelerometers for measuring real-world upper-limb performance in 20 stroke survivors with mild-to-moderate impairment, offering a more comprehensive assessment.
item.author: medRxiv
